title: Polynomial-Time Sharp Conditional Bounds in Dynamic Random-Coefficient Panels with Three Coefficient Types
banked_reason: The segment recursion and shared certificates establish sharp bounds in polynomial binary time for the stated three-type rational graph class, but the contribution remains a narrow computational specialization below the field floor.
gap_reasons: Lee’s broader conditional characterization already supplies the identification baseline, so the contribution is the computation and certificates under known coefficient support.
The four-type results prove a representation and coordinate-relaxation failure, while exact four-type complexity remains open; the framing states that limit accurately.

The only nonempty worked sharp interval has two periods, and the note supplies neither inference from sampled panels nor evidence of useful bounds in a richer nonempty dynamic design, limiting its leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an exact polynomial-time posterior-segment recursion and shared certificates for a calibrated finite rational dynamic-panel subclass with three known coefficient types, together with exact separation and representation counterexamples. The mathematics and citation audit passed, but the field-tier claim collapsed because the result remains a narrow computational specialization with only a two-period nonempty worked interval and no sampled-panel inference. A future re-raise must resolve the four-type complexity frontier, materially broaden the supported class, or add a substantive inference and dynamic-application layer.
tldr: For a supplied finite rational panel graph and three known persistent coefficient types, the full-history posterior recursion yields sharp conditional bounds and polynomial-size rational certificates. The four-type fixed-marginal coupling here has a two-dimensional posterior set, and separate coordinate intervals admit an impossible posterior. This locates the limit of the scalar endpoint representation; the complexity of richer exact four-type messages remains open. The positive algorithmic claim is confined to the calibrated finite-support subclass of Lee's model.
gap: Lee’s sharp characterization and Li’s fixed-marginal coupling analysis do not themselves give a graph-size binary algorithm for this conditional panel subclass. Bicausal transport and credal-tree message theorems have other coupling restrictions or maintained marginals, as the theorem-level matrix records.
fill: Prove the rank-one posterior segment theorem, exact graph-size primal-dual certificate construction, and a four-type failure of the scalar message. Use exact unconditional and information-coarsening gaps to explain why full conditioning matters.
